title: RPS-based Throughput Commitment and Adaptive Burst Allowance for Dedicated Pools
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a contract-ready, measurable throughput commitment expressed in requests-per-second (RPS) for Dedicated GPU pools, combined with an adaptive burst allowance that allows short-term capacity spikes without breaking downstream SLO expectations. Goal is to provide customers with a clean, developer-friendly guarantee (RPS floor + burst policy) that maps directly to autoscaler behavior, billing, and error-credit calculations.

Background: Existing deliverables focus on aggregate throughput bands and credit formulas that center on token-based or blended throughput metrics. Several enterprise customers have asked for an RPS-centric guarantee (their traffic is request-oriented rather than token-heavy) and for explicit, documented behavior when they exceed committed RPS for short windows. This ticket codifies an RPS-first SLA, the measurement method, how the autoscaler cooperates with contractual burst, and clear contract language for sales/legal.

Scope: Dedicated pools only. This ticket covers: definition of committed RPS target, short-term burst allowance and throttling semantics, error budget computation for RPS deficits, autoscaler policy contract interlock (how and when autoscaler is expected to scale), billing/credit language, monitoring/alerts instrumentation points, and docs for sales/legal. It intentionally excludes per-token pricing changes and per-model quality guarantees (handled elsewhere).

Non-goals: Introducing brand new billing units; support for multi-tenant shared dedicated pools; per-customer dynamic renegotiation tooling (manual only).
acceptance_criteria: SLA documented: committed RPS and burst allowance described in plain English plus math
Measurement spec implemented in metrics: rps_committed, rps_observed_1m, rps_99th_1h and burst_burn_rate
Credit calculation: automatic credit issuance workflow documented and reviewed with finance
Autoscaler interop: a policy exists that honors contractual burst windows and escalation thresholds
Legal-ready contract stub: paragraph for customer contracts reviewed by Legal
E2E test harness: synthetic workload test that demonstrates burst acceptance and crediting behavior
proposed_contract_language: Redwood agrees to maintain a committed throughput of X RPS ("Committed RPS") for the customer's Dedicated pool measured over rolling 1-hour windows at the 99th percentile.

Short-term bursts up to Y% above the Committed RPS are tolerated for windows up to Z minutes ("Burst Allowance"). Bursts beyond this allowance may be metered and billed, or curtailed per the throttling policy.

If observed Committed RPS (99th pct over 1h) falls below the contractual Committed RPS, customer will be eligible for service credits computed per the Credit Formula (see appendix). Credits are applied to the next billing cycle unless otherwise agreed.
Redwood will publish an incident and remediation plan when sustained degradation exceeds the error budget for more than two contiguous measurement windows.
measurement_method: Primary metric: rps_observed_1m (per-pool, per-customer) emitted by the ingress layer; aggregated to rps_99th_1h using sliding 1-hour windows of 1-minute samples.
Committed RPS compliance: compute the 99th percentile of rps_observed_1m over the last 60 samples; if that value < Committed RPS, the window is flagged as deficient.

Burst detection: compute rolling 5-minute averages and compare to Committed RPS; bursts > Burst Allowance for > Z minutes increment the burst_burn_rate counter used in crediting and autoscaler signals.

Error budget: defined as allowed_count_of_deficient_windows_per_30d (e.g., 3 windows/month). Each deficient 1-hour window consumes 1 error budget unit. Credits scale linearly with consumed units beyond allowance.
autoscaler_interop: Autoscaler will expose a contract mode: when a pool is contract-mode=true it will prioritize preserving customer Committed RPS by borrowing short-term cloud capacity (where available) up to the Burst Allowance before initiating throttling.
Scaling policy: when burst_burn_rate > threshold_A, autoscaler will trigger proactive scale-up with target headroom = max(Committed RPS*1.2, observed_peak).

Fallback: if cloud/infra capacity unavailable, autoscaler will gracefully degrade per the throttling policy (see throttling_behavior) and emit contract_degradation events into the console and billing pipeline.
Control plane knobs: fleet-level circuit-breaker can disable burst borrowing for customers flagged for risk (finance/account), tied to customer account settings.
throttling_behavior: Soft throttling: requests above allowed burst are served at increased latency by best-effort queuing for up to T seconds, after which queue-trimming begins.

Hard throttling: if observed RPS remains above Committed RPS + Burst Allowance for > 15 minutes and autoscaler cannot provision capacity, new requests will receive HTTP 429 with a well-documented retry-after header and explanation code.
Graceful degradation: Redwood will attempt model-fallback chaining to a smaller quantized variant (if configured by customer) before hard throttling, subject to model compatibility constraints.
billing_and_credit_formula: Credit unit: 1% of monthly committed fee credited per deficient 1-hour window beyond the monthly error budget allowance. Caps: credits do not exceed 100% of monthly committed fees per month.

Burst metering: bursts beyond Burst Allowance are recorded as billed overage units at the agreed overage rate; customers can opt into automatic overage billing or enforced throttling on contract signature.
Automatic issuance: credit events generate a billing ticket and a visible line-item in the customer's billing console; Finance receives an automated CSV export for reconciliation.
open_questions: Should Committed RPS be adjustable intra-contract (automated rerequests) or require a change-order? Current recommendation: manual change-order to avoid bill disputes.
What default values should we ship for Burst Allowance (Y%) and Z minutes? Proposals: 25% for 5 minutes (conservative) or 50% for 2 minutes (aggressive).
How to handle multi-az failover where traffic reroutes spike RPS in a single AZ — do we compute Committed RPS at global pool level or AZ-level?
design_feedback_and_reviews: 2026-03-05 - Design review (Ana Ribeiro): prefer a single global Committed RPS to avoid gaming across AZs; recommended adding an explicit cross-AZ failover allowance.
2026-03-08 - Legal review (Priya Nair): asked for clearer language around 'tolerated bursts' and recommended including explicit opt-in for overage billing vs enforced throttling.
2026-03-12 - Finance (Jordan Park): requested the credit formula include a de-minimis threshold to avoid micro-credits; suggested monthly rounding to nearest $10.
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (beta): offer to 3 trusted enterprise customers for validation; gate: metrics pipeline for rps_99th_1h and billing telemetry must be green.
Phase 2: enable self-serve in Console with default conservative Burst Allowance (25% for 5 minutes) and legal stub attached to provisioning flow.
Phase 3: general availability with API flags for change-order and optional auto-overage billing.
test_plan: Synthetic workload: spike tests at Committed RPS + 40% for 2, 5, 10, 20 minute durations to validate burst_burn_rate and autoscaler reactions.
Chaos test: simulate AZ drain and verify cross-AZ failover handling does not incorrectly consume monthly error budget when traffic moves predictably.
Billing integration: end-to-end verification that a deficient window generates a credit event visible in billing console and in finance CSV.
next_steps: Resolve open questions in architecture working group (target 2026-03-18).
Finalize default Burst Allowance parameters and encode them in autoscaler contract_mode implementation (ENG).
Produce legal-ready contract exhibit and get sign-off (Legal + Sales) by 2026-03-25.
